product: Unsulfured Blackstrap Molasses (ongoing microbial maintenance drench)
rate: 1-2 oz unsulfured molasses per gallon of water, applied as a soil drench alone or mixed directly into an alfalfa tea brew. Roughly 1 gallon of finished mix per 100 sq ft.
timing: Every 3-4 weeks during active growth, often combined with the alfalfa tea application day. During heat waves (95F+ for 3+ days) this is one of the few inputs safe to continue - use as a diluted 'stress drench' to help grass cope, alongside evening-only epsom salt foliar.
notes: This is a lower, ongoing-maintenance dose distinct from the one-time biochar-soap-molasses-soil-detox flush used to remediate chemically-sterilized soil at the start of a recovery project - see that recipe for the initial, higher-concentration detox ratio. Also distinct from fermented-rice-water-vs-molasses-soil-drench, which explains why molasses (not fermented rice water) is the practical choice for feeding soil bacteria at full-yard scale. Part of the rotating whole-lawn organic input schedule documented in annual-organic-lawn-care-rotation-brunswick-zone-9a.
